paragraph: Woodcliff Lake's single-family market is the main event, with 27 sales over six months at a median of $1,270,000 and a sale-to-list ratio of 1.02. Two thirds of those homes sold above asking and the median time to contract was 12 days, so this is a real seller's market and you should expect multiple offer situations on anything well presented. The typical sale is a four-bedroom colonial with three full baths. Sales ran from $210,000 to $2,200,000, and with a spread that wide the median is the number to anchor on. Townhouses and condos are a small, distinct slice at 8 sales, and the median of $1,295,000 sits slightly above the single-family median, so this isn't the cheaper option here. Seven of the eight were townhouses, they took a median 22 days, and the ratio of 0.98 says buyers had a little more room to negotiate. Monthly counts are too thin to read a trend from, though volume built through June the way it usually does before deep winter thins things out. If you're comparing the two, the deciding factor isn't price. It's whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family or the low-maintenance setup of a townhouse.
